audit.title: Secrets Management
audit.summary: This is a clear, well-structured conceptual page explaining how Chainlink Functions encrypts secrets via threshold encryption and the two hosting methods. Its biggest GEO strength is fluent, consistently-termed prose with liftable definitions; its biggest opportunity is that it stays purely conceptual — no comparison table for the two hosting methods, no code showing `Location.DONHosted` vs `Location.Remote` in use, and no symptom/how-to phrasing that developers actually query. Combined with absent page metadata (no JSON-LD, canonical, or dates), the page under-delivers on retrievability relative to the quality of its content. Honest verdict: solid explanation, weak agent-readiness.

recommendations.title: Add a hosting-methods comparison table
recommendations.issue: two methods buried in prose bullets — "DON-hosted (`Location.DONHosted`)… User-hosted (`Location.Remote`)"
recommendations.change: add a table with columns: Method · Enum value · Where ciphertext lives · Lifecycle owner · Minimum balance required · Best for. Keep the prose beneath.
recommendations.why: tables let engines extract *reasons* and build justified "which should I use" answers; this is the page's most-asked comparison.

recommendations.title: Add symptom/how-to phrased headings
recommendations.where: new H2s or a short FAQ
recommendations.issue: no headings match "how do I upload encrypted secrets to the DON" or "should I use DON-hosted or remote secrets"
recommendations.change: add sections/questions phrased exactly as devs query, each answered in the first sentence, linking to the how-to guides.
recommendations.why: concept-titled prose loses retrieval that question-phrased headings win, even when the answer is present.

recommendations.title: Add a code snippet showing secrets location config
recommendations.issue: 0 fenced code blocks; `Location.DONHosted`/`Location.Remote` shown only as inline names
recommendations.change: add a tagged JS/TS snippet (with imports) showing how each enum is passed when encrypting/uploading secrets, or link to the runnable example.
recommendations.why: agents completing secrets tasks need copy-pasteable config, not enum names in prose.

recommendations.title: Lead the "Threshold encryption" section with a definition
recommendations.issue: opens with "Using a single private key… poses a considerable security risk."
recommendations.change: prepend one liftable sentence: "Threshold encryption splits the master secret key into shares across DON nodes so that decrypting any secret requires at least K of N nodes to cooperate."
recommendations.why: a crisp first-sentence definition is what engines quote verbatim.

recommendations.title: Add external/primary citations
recommendations.change: inline-link the threshold-encryption scheme or Chainlink research/spec, and link "Byzantine nodes" to a canonical BFT definition.
recommendations.why: authoritative inline references raise credibility and citation rate.

recommendations.title: Replace vague quantifiers with specifics
recommendations.where: "considerable security risk," "corrupt a number of K nodes," "Some users prefer"
recommendations.issue: qualitative hedges where the K/F formulas already exist
recommendations.why: quantified claims are among the highest-lift changes; vague qualifiers underperform.

recommendations.title: Add page-level metadata
recommendations.issue: measured facts show no JSON-LD, no canonical, no dateModified
recommendations.change: emit `TechArticle` JSON-LD, a canonical URL, and a visible last-updated date.
recommendations.why: structured metadata and freshness signals improve parse trust and E-E-A-T (note: this may be a site-template fix, see below).

antiPatterns: Vague quantifiers: "considerable," "a number of," "some" — quantify or remove.
No undated/stale content flag possible: dates are simply absent, not stale.
No keyword stuffing, no marketing fluff, no unresolved cross-references — clean prose.
offPageNotes: Missing JSON-LD, canonical, and last-updated are likely **site-template** issues affecting all docs pages, not just this one — fix at the layout level.
`llms.txt` is already referenced at the top of the page — good site-level signal; verify it indexes this URL.
Head metadata could not be captured in this run; pass raw `<head>` via the CLI for a definitive metadata read.
